A short 2D platformer moth night meadow lanterns bats moon gate

Work in this order and check each step before the next:

3. Components and systems the game needs that the engine lacks go in the game module: edit it, then module_build (errors come back as file:line:col) and module_test.
4. Author the scenes with entity_create / component_set, save with scene_save, verify with run_headless (inspect, trace) and look with render_frame after every visible change.
5. Write .mctest scenarios under tests/ (a walk_to bot that must finish each level, no log errors) and run them with test_run; use playtest's feel report (stuck spots, deaths, idle time) to fix levels.

# 14. Working with an AI agent (MCP)

Every project has an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server (`<game>_mcp` from the checkout build, or
the stock `mce_mcp --module <lib<game>.so>`, `mce mcp` with the SDK) that gives an AI agent
the same scene-editing commands a person has in the editor, plus cook and headless verification.
Three games in the repository were authored entirely this way (Kindle's level, Prism Break and
Undertow), and a fourth (Lamplighter) by an agent that had never seen the engine source. This
chapter is the workflow that worked and the pitfalls it found.

## 14.1 Starting the server

```sh
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame --scene scenes/main.mcscene
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame --allow-cheats
build/<preset>/src/editor/mcp/mce_mcp --module build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/libmy_game.so --project projects/MyGame
mce mcp MyGame                                      # the SDK: the line above with its own paths
```

The server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin and stdout, one message per line (the MCP stdio
transport); it opens no socket. Stdout carries nothing else: logs go to stderr, and so does the
command line `mce mcp` prints before it starts the server. Use the **project's** server or the stock one **with the module**:

# 7. 2D games

The 2D path is a set of scene-authored components (the "kit") that the player draws for you:
sprites, text, a camera, parallax layers, 2D lights, post effects, tilemap layers and particle
emitters. Your game code changes their fields; nothing in your module draws.

Units are metres with +Y up. An entity's `LocalTransform` places the sprite's pivot, its rotation
about Z turns the quad, and its scale multiplies `size`.

## 7.1 Sprites

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `texture` | the image; a null reference draws a solid quad in `tint` |
| `normal_map` | tangent-space normal map for 2D lighting (import with `srgb: false`) |
| `tint` | colour multiplier in **linear** RGB (see below); `tint.a` fades the sprite |
| `size` | world size in metres; the texture is stretched to it |
| `pivot` | normalized, `[0.5, 0.5]` centre, `[0, 0]` bottom-left |
| `layer`, `order` | stacking: `layer` first (−100..100), then `order` within the layer, then ECS order |
| `flip_x`, `flip_y` | mirror |
| `region` | the part of the texture shown, `[u0, v0, u1, v1]` from 0 to 1 with `v0` the top edge; `[0, 0, 1, 1]` (the default) is the whole texture |

`region` picks a frame out of an atlas by hand; an `AnimatedSprite` (7.3) writes it for you.
Missing or broken textures draw as a magenta checker rather than nothing.

# 10. Audio

Audio is a 48 kHz stereo float mixer on its own thread with 48 real voices, buses with EQ and a
limiter, sample-accurate scheduling and 3D attenuation. From a game you touch it in three ways: an
`AudioSource` component for sounds that belong to an entity, a `PlaySfx` event for one-shots, and
convars for the bus volumes.

## 10.1 Sounds that belong to an entity

```json
"Torch": {
  "LocalTransform": { "position": [4, 1, 0] },
  "AudioSource": { "clip": "guid:<crackle.wav>", "loop": true, "play_on_start": true, "gain_db": -6 }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `clip` | the `.wav` asset |
| `gain_db`, `pan` | −60..12 dB, −1..1 |
| `priority` | 0..255; louder and higher priority voices survive when voices run out |
| `bus` | `Master`, `Music`, `SFX` (default) or `UI` (`audio::AudioBus`; scenes written with the number, `"bus": 1`, still load). `Music` streams the clip in 100 ms pages instead of holding it decoded (two music streams at a time; a third plays from memory) |
| `loop` | gapless; the clip's loop points come from the WAV's own markers or the sidecar's `loop_start` / `loop_end` |
| `play_on_start` | start when the entity appears |
| `fade_s` | seconds the voice fades in when it starts and out when the component or entity is removed |

Changing `gain_db` or `pan` from code ramps over 10 ms (no clicks). Removing the component stops
the voice with a short fade (`fade_s` when it is longer). Music is a looping `AudioSource` on the
